facts.text: UR5TaskSpaceEnv subclasses ur5_env.UR5Env in ur_openai.task_envs.ur5_task_space.
The task-env registry registers UR5TaskSpaceEnv-v0 with entry point ur_openai.task_envs.ur5_task_space:UR5TaskSpaceEnv and a max_episode_steps argument.
The simulation task-space configuration sets env_id UR5TaskSpaceEnv-v0 and agent_control_dt 0.005 s.
The same configuration sets n_actions 3 and distance_threshold 5.0.
The action space is Box(-1., 1.) with shape (n_actions,) and dtype float32.
The observation space is an unbounded Box whose shape is the observation built in __init__.
The observation concatenates joint angles, end-effector pose, target pose, pose error and velocity.
The pose error is translation_rotation_error(target_pose, end-effector pose) and the velocity is a finite difference over agent_control_dt.
For n_actions 3, the action is multiplied by 0.001 and applied as a translation-only pose delta with zero rotation delta.
_set_action sends the command with set_target_pose_flex(cmd, t=agent_control_dt) without checking its return value, publishes the current pose and sleeps on the loop rate.
The loop rate is rospy.Rate(1/agent_control_dt).
The reward is 100.0 when the episode is done and otherwise the negative end-effector-to-target distance times 1000.
Termination is true when the translational error converted to millimetres is below distance_threshold.

RobotGazeboEnv.step calls _pause_env when the pause flag is set, then unpause, _set_action and pause on the robot connection, reads the observation, computes terminated, truncated (step_count >= 200) and reward, and returns a five-tuple.
RobotGazeboEnv.reset accepts seed and options, updates the episode, initializes per-episode variables, resets the simulation and returns (observation, info).
RobotGazeboEnv.seed reseeds np_random with gymnasium.utils.seeding.np_random.
With reset_controls false, RobotGazeboEnv._reset_sim calls unpause, _check_all_systems_ready, _set_init_pose, pause, reset, unpause, _check_all_systems_ready and pause on the robot connection.
With random_target_pose and random_initial_pose enabled, _set_init_pose redraws the target around the current pose and samples a new start pose from the workspace.
The simulation task-space configuration enables random_target_pose and random_initial_pose.
The README describes the project as a Universal Robot Environment for Gymnasium and ROS Gazebo.
get_robot_params loads the ur_gym parameters, reads ur_gym/driver without a default and sets param_use_gazebo to False whatever the driver value is.
UR5Env passes param_use_gazebo as use_gazebo, with reset_controls False, to RobotGazeboEnv, then calls robot_connection.unpause and constructs ur_control's Arm.
RobotGazeboEnv uses GazeboConnection only when use_gazebo is true; otherwise it uses RobotConnection and subscribes to ur3/pause.
RobotConnection's pause, unpause and reset do nothing.
pause_callback sets the pause flag when a ur3/pause message is true.
UR5Env._pause_env reads the joint angles, blocks on input('Press Enter to continue') and then moves the arm back to those angles with wait=True.
_set_action calls sys.exit() when the action contains NaN and asserts that every value lies within -1.0001 and 1.0001.
RobotGazeboEnv.close calls rospy.signal_shutdown.
Importing ur5_env inserts an absolute /home/imr workspace path at the front of sys.path.
Arm publishes its flexible trajectories on the namespace plus '/' plus JOINT_PUBLISHER_ROBOT plus '/command'.
JOINT_PUBLISHER_ROBOT is scaled_pos_joint_traj_controller.
The ur_gazebo UR5 controller configuration defines a controller named scaled_pos_joint_traj_controller.

set_joint_positions_flex returns SPEED_LIMIT_EXCEEDED without commanding when the required joint speed exceeds max_joint_speed, and set_target_pose_flex returns IK_NOT_FOUND when inverse kinematics finds no solution.
With curriculum_learning enabled, each _set_init_pose call lowers dist_cl by 0.005 and uses it as distance_threshold, never below 5.
The simulation task-space configuration sets driver gazebo, curriculum_learning true and dist_cl 50.
UR5PickAndPlaceRealEnv.get_robot_params sets param_use_gazebo True unless the ur_gym/driver parameter is robot.
The real-robot configuration sets env_id UR5PickAndPlaceRealEnv-v0 and driver robot.

determinism.notes: the fake draws its target jitter from random.Random(seed) at reset, so one seed repeats; upstream reset(seed) ignores the seed and redraws the target and start pose from the process-global numpy RNG, so a seed does not reproduce an upstream trajectory

gaps: the checked fake is an analytic kinematic stand-in for the ROS/Gazebo environment: it translates the end-effector by 0.001 m per unit action in a straight line and models no inverse kinematics, joint limits, dynamics, contacts, collisions, grasping, Gazebo physics or ROS graph

no ROS or Gazebo run: the upstream environment needs ROS Noetic, Gazebo, a catkin workspace and the clone's ur_control, ur_gazebo and ur_pykdl packages, none of which were installed where the gate ran

the upstream reset(seed) ignores the seed and redraws the target around the current pose and the start pose from the workspace with the process-global numpy RNG; the fake uses its own seed-local jitter, so the two give different episodes

the fake's 32-element observation mirrors the upstream concatenation of 6 joint angles + 7 end-effector pose + 7 target pose + 6 pose error + 6 velocity, but the joint angles and orientation are placeholders and no forward kinematics is modelled
the environment cannot be constructed before a ROS node and ROS parameters exist; the implicit sim backend gym.make('UR5TaskSpaceEnv-v0') was not run and needs the upstream register_environment call

live construction in the server process would read ur_gym/driver without a default, insert an absolute /home/imr path into sys.path on import, construct ur_control's Arm and create ROS publishers; a NaN action makes _set_action call sys.exit(), a true ur3/pause message makes the next step block on input(), and close() calls rospy.signal_shutdown

upstream get_robot_params leaves param_use_gazebo False for every driver value, so UR5TaskSpaceEnv uses the no-op RobotConnection: it never pauses or resets Gazebo, and its Arm commands scaled_pos_joint_traj_controller, the controller name that ur_gazebo and the real UR driver share, so the same class moves a real UR5 when the operator's ROS graph runs the real driver

set_target_pose_flex can return IK_NOT_FOUND or SPEED_LIMIT_EXCEEDED without commanding the arm, and _set_action ignores the return value, so an upstream step can complete without motion; the fake models neither

the shipped simulation configuration enables curriculum_learning, so upstream _set_init_pose uses dist_cl (50, lowered by 0.005 per reset, never below 5) as the termination threshold and draws the target within n_count * 0.001 m of the current pose; the fake keeps the fixed 5.0 mm threshold and a placeholder target, so its episode lengths differ
the fake applies the upstream step_count >= 200 truncation itself; the gymnasium TimeLimit wrapper that gym.make can add was not exercised (the training scripts use .unwrapped)
snapshot and restore are not offered: the upstream environment has no get_state/set_state methods
the runtime latch stops future step/reset calls but cannot interrupt one in-flight native env.step; this is a simulation latch, not a physical emergency stop

measures.description: Last observation (derived from the observation space)
measures.name: observation

safe_state.description: software latch only: after an e-stop no further step or reset is accepted until mhs.safety.reset clears the latch, an in-flight native step may finish and the last observation stays readable. Upstream UR5TaskSpaceEnv never pauses Gazebo (it always uses the no-op RobotConnection), so a live simulation keeps running and the trajectory controller holds the last commanded target. The latch sends no zero trajectory and does not stop a UR arm on scaled_pos_joint_traj_controller/command
